stops.name: Sainte-Catherine-de-Fierbois, Joan halts at the shrine
stops.campa: Eleven days out of Vaucouleurs, through enemy country in a man's clothes, Joan the Maid comes to rest at the one shrine on her road that bears her counselor's name. At Sainte-Catherine-de-Fierbois she hears three Masses in a day and dictates her first letter to the Dauphin at Chinon, six leagues on: she has ridden a hundred and fifty leagues to come to his aid, and she knows many things good for him. She sleeps under Catherine's roof, above the buried sword, and says nothing of it yet. Her voices keep their own calendar.

stops.name: Tours, the armorer is sent
stops.campa: At Tours, armed and examined and believed, the Maid refuses the offer of a new sword. Her voices have told her where hers lies: in the church of Saint Catherine at Fierbois, behind the altar, in the ground. She sends an armorer of Tours with a letter to the priests of Fierbois asking that the sword be sought and sent. She has never seen the man who buried it nor the earth that holds it. The clergy of Fierbois take up the pavement behind their altar because a peasant girl wrote to them that a sword was there.
stops.quote: Whilst I was at Tours, or at Chinon, I sent to seek for a sword which was in the Church of Saint Catherine de Fierbois, behind the altar; it was found there at once; the sword was in the ground, and rusty; upon it were five crosses; I knew by my Voice where it was.
stops.quote_source: Joan of Arc, trial testimony, Rouen, 27 February 1431

stops.name: Sainte-Catherine-de-Fierbois, the sword found: the circle closes
stops.campa: The priests dig behind the altar and the earth gives up the blade: rusted through, five crosses on the steel. They rub it, and the rust falls away at once, without effort: a thousand years of waiting shed like a husk. The clergy of Fierbois sheath it in red velvet; Joan will carry it to Orléans and Patay and never, she swears, kill a man with it. Here the journey ends and hands itself on: the wisdom of Alexandria, burned at Cinaron, crowned at Sinai, carried to Normandy, has put its sword into the hand of the girl. Catherine's road ends where Joan's begins.
stops.quote: After this sword was found, the prelates of the place had it rubbed, and at once the rust fell from it without difficulty.
stops.quote_source: Joan of Arc, trial testimony, Rouen, 27 February 1431
